project.objective: Did Friedrich Carl Weber and his wife Catharina Carell of Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau have a daughter named Anna Maria Eva, born 1870?

questions.question: Is there a birth or baptismal record documenting the birth of a daughter named Anna Maria Eva to Friedrich Carl Weber and Catharina Carell in Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau, circa 1870?
questions.rationale: The project objective asks whether this specific child existed. Sindlingen was a Catholic parish in the Diocese of Limburg; baptismal registers survive in the Hesse-Nassau diocesan collections on FamilySearch and likely include entries for children of this couple married there in February 1869. A birth/baptismal record from circa 1870 would directly confirm or refute the claim.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two original church records (Kirchenbuch D43H-7DN2 and Kirchenbuchduplikat D43D-J2MM, collection 3479701) directly name Anna Maria Eva Weber born 26 Feb 1870, baptized 13 Mar 1870, as daughter of Karl Weber and Katharina Karell, identified as GTDL-981 and GTD2-RXP. A sibling baptism record (Rosina Weber, D4WC-V9PZ, 3 May 1869) independently confirms the couple's identity and Nied/Höchst parish. Church baptism is the only primary record class for a birth in pre-civil-registration Hesse-Nassau (civil registration introduced 1874); all available record types for this jurisdiction and era have been searched. Multiple name variants (Friedrich Carl / Carl Friedrich / Karl, Catharina / Catharina Karel / Katharina Karell) and place variants (Sindlingen, Nied, Höchst, broad Hesse-Nassau) were tried. pli_002, pli_003, and pli_005 skipped as fallbacks superseded by successful primary search.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes — two primary records directly name Anna Maria Eva Weber as daughter of the subject couple born 26 Feb 1870. Question fully answered.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FamilySearch collection 3479701 (Diocese of Limburg Kirchenbücher) searched with multiple name and place variants. FAN/sibling search executed (pli_004). Secondary and fallback items (pli_002, pli_003, pli_005) skipped because the primary search succeeded and civil registration did not begin in Hesse-Nassau until 1874 — no additional primary record type exists for a 1870 birth.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Both index entries followed to original record content via record_read. Kirchenbuch (original church register) and Kirchenbuchduplikat (original civil copy) both accessed.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Kirchenbuch and Kirchenbuchduplikat share informants (presenting parents) and constitute one evidence unit for the Anna Maria Eva Weber baptism. The Rosina Weber baptism (D4WC-V9PZ, 1869) independently corroborates the couple's identity in the same parish. Maximum independence achievable given a single birth event in pre-civil-registration Hesse-Nassau.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Kirchenbuch is an original record. Father present at baptism — primary informant for his own identity and parentage; secondary informant for child's birth date/place. Kirchenbuchduplikat is an original civil copy. Evidence is direct for child's name, parentage, and baptism.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: No conflicts. Both records agree on child's name (Anna Maria Eva Weber), birth date (26 Feb 1870), baptism date (13 Mar 1870), father (Karl Weber = GTDL-981), and mother (Katharina Karell = GTD2-RXP).
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. No civil birth certificate exists for a 1870 Hesse-Nassau birth (civil registration starts 1874). No name-indexed German household census covers 1870. No other record type expected to name a different parent. pli_002 would index the same underlying records differently — cannot change the facts found. The two-record finding is stable and the couple's identity is corroborated by a third independent record.

items.rationale: The primary source for a Sindlingen Catholic baptism circa 1870. FamilySearch collection 3479701 ('Germany, Hessen-Nassau, Diocese of Limburg, Catholic Church Records, 1601-1919') is name-indexed with 1.5 million records and covers Sindlingen's Kirchenbuch (Taufen 1818-1876, film 008640565) and its civil duplicate Kirchenbuchduplikat (Geburten 1818-1874, film 008640567). An 1870 birth predates Prussian civil registration in Hesse-Nassau (which began 1874), so this is the sole primary source class. The couple's 1869 marriage is already indexed in this same collection (ARKs D4WX-91PZ, D4HV-K63Z), confirming Sindlingen records are present. Search for female children of Friedrich Carl Weber and Catharina Carell born 1869-1872.

FamilySearch collection 1768560 ('Germany, Hesse-Nassau, Civil Registers and Church Books, 1701-1930', 234,902 indexed records) provides a second access path to Hesse-Nassau church and civil records. It may contain Sindlingen entries indexed under different standardPlace conventions, or may include extracted entries from the Kirchenbuchduplikat not yet surfaced by collection 3479701. Searching this as a secondary check catches any coverage gaps between the two collections.

Fallback for item 1: if the name-indexed search in collection 3479701 returns no result, browse the Sindlingen baptismal register image-by-image. ImageGroup 008640565_004_M9X1-4Y6 covers Taufen 1844-1876 (0% name-indexed, German Kurrent script). Browse the pages corresponding to 1869-1872 directly to check for an Anna Maria Eva Weber entry missed by the index — indexer errors and name variants are common in this period. Note the film is listed under the Duchy of Nassau standardPlace even though the records span into the Prussian period; both FamilySearch place designations refer to the same physical register. Routed via search-images skill.

FAN / sibling search: search collection 3479701 more broadly for all children baptized in Sindlingen to Friedrich Carl Weber and Catharina Carell across the 1865-1880 range. This establishes the couple's documented family pattern — how many children appear in the registers, whether any other children cluster around 1870, and whether Anna Maria Eva appears under a slightly different name spelling. A family with no documented children is itself evidence worth recording; siblings found would corroborate the couple's presence in Sindlingen during the target period.

External paid fallback: Ancestry collection dbid=61117 ('Hesse, Germany, Births, 1851-1901') may contain extracted birth records from Hesse-Nassau that overlap the Sindlingen registers or provide an index entry for an Anna Weber born circa 1870. Search only if FamilySearch searches (items 1-3) are inconclusive. Requires an Ancestry subscription.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Anna Maria Eva Weber: Probable Daughter of Friedrich Carl Weber and Catharina Carell

**Question:** Did Friedrich Carl Weber and his wife Catharina Carell of Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau have a daughter named Anna Maria Eva, born 1870?

**Conclusion (Probable):** The evidence strongly suggests that Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 February 1870 and baptized 13 March 1870 at Höchst, Hessen-Nassau, Prussia, is the daughter of Friedrich Carl Weber (born 1846) and his wife Catharina Carell (born 14 February 1847), who had married 7 February 1869 at Sindlingen, Kreis Höchst, Hessen-Nassau.

### Evidence

**Kirchenbuch entry (original church register):** The Catholic baptismal register of the Diocese of Limburg records Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 February 1870, baptized 13 March 1870, as the daughter of Karl Weber (father) and Katharina Karell (mother).[^1] The officiating priest created this record at the time of the baptismal ceremony — an original source. The presenting parents attended in person and supplied the child's name and birth date; accordingly, the parentage assertions carry primary information and the christening fact is primary evidence of the baptism. This entry is direct evidence for the child's name, birth date, baptismal place, and parentage.

**Kirchenbuchduplikat (original civil duplicate):** A separately created civil duplicate of the same baptismal act records Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 February 1870, daughter of Karl Weber and Katharina Karell.[^2] Required by Hesse-Nassau civil law from 1818, the Kirchenbuchduplikat is an original document created for civil authority registration — independent of the Kirchenbuch in its institutional destination, but sharing the same presenting parents and officiating priest as informants. It agrees on all material points: child's name, birth date, and parents. Because both records derive from the same baptismal event and the same informants, they constitute one evidence unit for GPS independence purposes.

**Corroborating sibling baptism:** A Catholic baptismal register entry for Rosina Weber, baptized 3 May 1869 at Nied, Höchst, Hessen-Nassau, names Carl Friedrich Weber (father) and Catharina Karel (mother).[^3] Rosina died the same day. This record — approximately ten months before Anna Maria Eva's birth — independently establishes this couple in the Nied/Höchst parish before the target birth. It does not directly name Anna Maria Eva Weber, but it corroborates the couple's identity and their presence in the relevant parish across a different original record and a different baptismal event.

### Name Variants and Identity Resolution

The father appears in three name forms: 'Karl Weber' in both baptism records for Anna Maria Eva, and 'Carl Friedrich Weber' in the Rosina Weber record. The tree carries this individual as Friedrich Carl Weber (GTDL-981, born 1846). These forms reflect two conventions common in German Catholic registers of this period: the use of the Rufname (the daily-life name, here 'Carl' / 'Karl') in place of the formal first given name 'Friedrich,' and variation in the ordering of given-name elements. The wife's consistent co-occurrence across all three records confirms a single identity: 'Katharina Karell' (Kirchenbuch), 'Katharina Karell' (Kirchenbuchduplikat), and 'Catharina Karel' (Rosina Weber baptism) are orthographic variants of 'Catharina Carell' (GTD2-RXP, born 14 February 1847). The couple's marriage on 7 February 1869 places the birth of Anna Maria Eva on 26 February 1870 — approximately twelve months later — within the expected range.

### Search Scope

Research was conducted primarily in FamilySearch collection 3479701 ('Germany, Hessen-Nassau, Diocese of Limburg, Catholic Church Records, 1601-1919'), the primary indexed repository for Catholic baptisms in the Diocese of Limburg, which encompasses both the Sindlingen and Höchst/Nied parishes where this family's records are found. Prussia did not introduce civil birth registration in Hesse-Nassau until 1 January 1874; no civil birth certificate therefore exists for a birth of February 1870 in this jurisdiction. Multiple name and place variants were searched. A sibling search yielded the Rosina Weber record, which was instrumental in identifying the family's Nied parish and the father's indexed name form. A secondary collection (1768560) and image-browse and Ancestry fallbacks were assessed as redundant after the primary search succeeded and were skipped. Research was declared reasonably exhaustive.

### GPS Component Assessment

| Component | Status |
|---|---|
| Reasonably exhaustive research | Declared |
| Complete and accurate citations | Citations copied verbatim from research.json |
| Analysis and correlation | Three records correlated; name variants resolved |
| Resolution of conflicting evidence | No conflicts — all records agree on material facts |
| Soundly reasoned conclusion | This summary |

**Tier: probable.** The conclusion is limited to probable rather than proved because the Kirchenbuch and Kirchenbuchduplikat share informants and constitute one evidence unit; a second independently informanted source directly naming Anna Maria Eva as the daughter of this couple has not been located. This constraint is inherent to the jurisdictional record landscape: civil registration began in 1874, leaving the church baptism register as the only primary record class for a 1870 birth in Hesse-Nassau. The strong preponderance of available evidence supports the conclusion. A future record independently naming Anna Maria Eva — such as a census household entry, a sibling's marriage record naming the Weber parents, or an emigration or death record — could advance the tier to proved.

## Locality Guide: Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau — circa 1870

### Jurisdictional Context
Sindlingen in 1870 lay in the former Duchy of Nassau, annexed by Prussia in 1866 and incorporated into the Province of Hesse-Nassau. FamilySearch standard places: 'Sindlingen, Frankfurt, Duchy of Nassau' (pre-1866) and 'Sindlingen, Höchst, Hesse-Nassau, Prussia, Germany' (from 1886). Sindlingen was a Catholic parish in the Diocese of Limburg (Bistum Limburg), organized 1827.

### Key Records
**1. Diocese of Limburg Catholic Church Records (PRIMARY, INDEXED)**
- FS collection 3479701: 1,512,303 indexed records; 301,321 images
- Sindlingen Taufen 1818-1876 on film 008640565 (imageGroup 008640565_004_M9X1-4Y6)
- Also: Heiraten 1844-1880, Tote 1818-1874, Kommunionen 1835-1902 on film 008640566
- Civil duplicate (Kirchenbuchduplikat): Geburten/Heiraten 1818-1874 on film 008640567

**2. Browse-only volumes** (same films, 0% indexed): must be read image-by-image

**3. Germany, Hesse-Nassau, Civil Registers and Church Books, 1701-1930** (FS 1768560): 234,902 indexed records — secondary check

**4. Civil Registration** — NOT applicable: Hesse-Nassau Prussian civil registration began 1874; 1870 birth predates it

**5. Germany Births and Baptisms, 1558-1898** (FS 1473000): broad catch-all

**6. External repositories**: Landesarchiv Hessen; Diocesan Archives Limburg (archiv@bistumlimburg.de); Ancestry 'Hesse, Germany, Births, 1851-1901' (dbid=61117)

### Research Approach
Search FS collection 3479701 first (name-indexed). If no indexed result, browse imageGroup 008640565_004_M9X1-4Y6 (Taufen 1818-1876) image-by-image.
